chunks: And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Fudhayl ibn Uthman, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, blessings of Allah be upon them both, he said:
The Commander of the Believers, blessings of Allah be upon him, used to say: "No act performed with taqwa is little. And how can that which is accepted (by Allah) be called little?!"

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Amir al-Mu'minin: Commander of the Believers, title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.التقوى: Taqwa: God-consciousness, piety, mindful awareness of Allah in all actions
key_terms.صلوات الله عليه: Salawat Allah alayhi: blessings of Allah be upon him
key_terms.عمل: Amal: deed, action, work done in worship or daily life
key_terms.يتقبل: Yutaqabbal: is accepted (by Allah); divine acceptance of righteous deeds

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about deeds performed with taqwa?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of al-Mufid, Imam al-Baqir (AS) reports that Imam Ali, the Commander of the Believers (AS), used to say that no act done with taqwa (God-consciousness) is insignificant, posing the rhetorical question: how can something that Allah accepts ever be considered little? This teaching, transmitted through a chain from the Imam's circle in Kufa, underscores the Shia ethical principle that sincerity and piety transform even the smallest deed into something immense in divine reckoning. The original audience of scholars and students of hadith would have understood taqwa not merely as fear of God, but as a comprehensive awareness of the divine presence that permeates every action.
